doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Frank Butler, Billy Higgins and the next wave of LA drummers
summary: Hamilton and Brown discuss Frank Butler, the most-recorded drummer Billy Higgins and Earl Palmer, whom Hamilton did not see coming up.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: How about some of the other drummers that came out of LA like Frank Butler? He’s younger then you?
Frank Butler was a good player. I didn’t get a chance to hear that much, just like I didn’t hear what’s his name?
Oh, I know Lawrence, but who just passed -- had a club -­
No. I think the last thing he did, he did with Charles Lloyd. What’s his name? He’s supposed to be the most recorded drummer.
That goes to Bernard Purdy saying he’s -­
You were there when Earl Palmer came though?
He always smiled when he played. Billy Higgins.
Billy Higgins, oh, yeah, Higgins. So you didn’t see them coming up?
No, you’d already -- yeah they all came out and that’s our next wave after you. Well Lawrence I guess is kind of in between.
Yeah, well I heard Lawrence when he was -­

Yeah, and then there’s Billy Higgins, yeah. Again, trailblazing, you were the first one to come out and fly that coop. Okay, well let’s see, a teacher. Let’s talk about the Parson School and getting involved in teaching.
